rejected.summary: description: Use when a user wants guidance on starting, contributing to, growing, governing, funding, securing, or sustaining an open source project, or asks about contributor onboarding, community health, maintainer burnout, code of conduct, metrics, legal basics, or open source project adoption.
Use the official Open Source Guides as a coaching framework for open source questions.
- Use the official Open Source Guides site: <https://opensource.guide/>
- decide whether or how to open source a project
- understand open source legal basics
- deep software security implementation guidance unrelated to open source project operations
- do not write a full `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- do not write a governance charter
- do not write a code of conduct
- Burnout, boundaries, maintainership balance: `maintaining-balance-for-open-source-maintainers`
- Maintainer overload + burnout: `best-practices` + `maintaining-balance-for-open-source-maintainers`
- `starting-a-project` -> `Starting an Open Source Project`
You are an early-stage solo maintainer deciding whether your side project is ready for open source.
**Starting an Open Source Project**
If you want to think about early contributor experience, read How to Contribute to Open Source next.
This skill is based on the official Open Source Guides project and should keep attribution attached to the source material it summarizes.
- Open Source Guides site: <https://opensource.guide/>
- <https://opensource.guide/maintaining-balance-for-open-source-maintainers/>
Per the upstream README, Open Source Guides content is released under `CC-BY-4.0`.
# Open Source Guides Map
Use this file to route open source questions to the smallest useful set of official guide topics.

| `starting-a-project`                              | Starting an Open Source Project                 | Someone is deciding whether to open source a project or wants to prepare for launch.                            | "should I open source this", "what do I need before launch", "how do I start"      | <https://opensource.guide/starting-a-project/>

| `how-to-contribute`                               | How to Contribute to Open Source                | The user wants better contributor onboarding or wants to help with an open source project.                      | "how can people contribute", "first contribution", "new contributor path"          | <https://opensource.guide/how-to-contribute/>

| `getting-paid`                                    | Getting Paid for Open Source Work               | The user is exploring sustainability, sponsorship, grants, or business support for the project.                 | "funding", "sponsor", "how do we sustain this", "can maintainers get paid"         | <https://opensource.guide/getting-paid/>

| `metrics`                                         | Open Source Metrics                             | The user wants to measure project health, impact, contributor flow, or growth without guessing.                 | "what should we measure", "metrics", "health indicators", "success"                | <https://opensource.guide/metrics/>

| `legal`                                           | The Legal Side of Open Source                   | The user has licensing or legal-basics questions about operating an open source project.                        | "license", "legal", "can I use this", "what should we choose"                      | <https://opensource.guide/legal/>

| `maintaining-balance-for-open-source-maintainers` | Maintaining Balance for Open Source Maintainers | A maintainer is overwhelmed, burned out, or struggling to protect time and energy.                              | "burned out", "too much maintenance", "need a break", "exhausted"                  | <https://opensource.guide/maintaining-balance-f
